drafts.subject: chr:entity:mark-antony
drafts.quotation: Antony made it clear to all the world that he was swayed by the sentiments neither of a commander nor of a brave man, nor even by his own, but, as someone in pleasantry said that the soul of the lover dwells in another’s body, he was dragged along by the woman
drafts.rationale: The passage follows Cleopatra's ships sailing off through the fighting line towards Peloponnesus. It says Antony was dragged along by 'the woman' (Cleopatra) and acted neither as a commander nor a brave man, which shows him leaving the engagement in flight. The battle is not named in this passage; it is identified from the surrounding sea-fight narrative, so this claim leans on context.
ambiguities: The target passage does not name the battle; the link to the Battle of Actium comes from context. Antony's flight is implied here and made explicit only in 66.5.
reasons: ambiguity: The target passage does not name the battle; the link to the Battle of Actium comes from context. Antony's flight is implied here and made explicit only in 66.5.
